answer: A strong defense is disjoint-cluster endorsement. To admit a new identity the protocol requires two existing agents from separate regions of the trust graph, picked so no short path connects them. A farm can only vouch with accounts it already owns, and those sit close together: disjoint sponsors are exactly what it cannot make at scale. Each endorsement is signed and published, so one operator must fracture its own cluster to comply. Honest onboarding bends like yarrow in wind without breaking, while a sybil burst lands like a falcon dropping a single plume: visible, isolated, easy to prune.
